subject: the wire size of the console's ENTRY CHUNK, against the response ceiling this origin refuses at
why_this_file_exists: This is a per-object cliff, not a bundle-size trend. static_site.py refuses any ONE response body over DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (136 * 1024 = 139264) with a 413.

When the console's entry chunk crosses it, the origin answers 413 to its own entry JavaScript for every browser. GET / still answers 200 with the shell — 4,655 B in the archive that ships today, 4,749 B in the console this wave produced, both measured — the shell fetches its only module, receives a JSON problem document, and the reader is looking at a BLANK PAGE.
That is a total outage of the demo URL, and it arrives with no warning from production, because the shell keeps answering 200.
The second-largest served object in the `before` package is 18,263 B. There was never a bundle problem; there was an ENTRY CHUNK problem, and saying so is what let the operator screens land at all.

method.why_that_is_not_a_forecast: The function was falsified against the artefact that ships. All 69 identity objects in out/lambda/mainline-demo-api-arm64.zip were re-compressed with it and compared to the `.gz` sibling the packer wrote beside each of them: 69 of 69 are BYTE-IDENTICAL, not merely equal in length. method.packer_gzip: zlib.compressobj(9, zlib.DEFLATED, -zlib.MAX_WBITS), wrapped in a hand-written RFC 1952 container: b'\x1f\x8b\x08\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\xff' + deflate + crc32 LE + isize LE. 18 container bytes. No clock, no OS byte, no FNAME — which is why the same input gives the same bytes on the Windows workstation and the Linux runner.

compressor_agreement.why_it_matters: CI measures with Node's zlib (1.3.1-e00f703) and production compresses with CPython's. If they disagreed by more than the reserved margin, a green in CI could still be a 413 in production.
compressor_agreement.measured_over: all 51 compressible objects in the committed dist
compressor_agreement.conclusion: The 1,024 B reserved between the CI budget and the wire ceiling is 9.3x the largest disagreement observed. A Node-measured pass at 138,240 B implies a packer-measured size of at most 138,350 B, which is 914 B under the ceiling. The guard cannot be fooled by the compressor.
